claims.source_quote_ar: الطاغوت: كعب بن الأشرف، سماه اللَّه «طاغوتا» لإفراطه في الطغيان وعداوة رسول اللَّه صلى اللَّه عليه وسلم. أو على التشبيه بالشيطان
claims.claim_ar: تسميتهم «الطاغوت» كناية/استعارة عن المُستبدّ/المُعاند، بحيث يُشبَّه الشخص بالطاغوت/الشيطان (كناية بلاغية).
claims.claim_en: Calling someone 'al-Taghut' functions as a kinayah/metaphor, likening that person to a tyrant/satanic figure.

claims.source_quote_ar: نزلت في رجل من المنافقين يقال له: بشر.
claims.claim_ar: ثَمَّ تضادّ/طباق بين ادعائهم الإيمان (يَزْعُمُونَ أَنَّهُمْ آمَنُوا) وأفعالهم التي تميل لِلطُغيان أو الكفر (أَنْ يَكْفُرُوا بِهِ/أَنْ يَتَحَاكَمُوا إِلَى الطَّاغُوتِ)؛ أي وجود تناقض بين القول والفعل يخلق طباقاً بلاغياً.
claims.claim_en: There is an antithesis (tibaq) between their claim of belief and their actions (seeking judgment to Taghut / being commanded to disbelieve), producing a rhetorical antithesis between professed faith and contrary conduct.
claims.needs_review_reason: The cited chunk mentions a hypocrite episode and supports a theme of hypocrisy/contradiction, but it does not quote the exact contrasted phrases from this ayah; linkage is interpretive and should be reviewed.

warnings: Source chunks provided are excerpts of tafsir (primarily Zamakhshari-related) and do not contain the full ayah text; some rhetorical readings (e.g., interrogative opening 'أَلَمْ تَرَ' as an enáctive interrogative device) cannot be directly supported from these chunks and were therefore not extracted.

Only claims for which an exact substring exists in the provided chunks were produced. Interpretive claims that rely on the ayah's internal word-pairs but lack an explicit citation in the chunks were given lower confidence or omitted.

Fields 'root' and 'lemma' for ayah-level claims may be composite (e.g., 'زعم/كفر') when the rhetorical contrast spans multiple lexical items; please review and split if per-word roots/lemmas are required.
